parsed.title: The arbitrary-group induced removal conjecture
parsed.statement:
Fix a bipartite graph $F$, and let $G$ be a finite group. A subset $A \subseteq G$ is **$\epsilon$-far from bi-induced-$F$-free** if changing fewer than $\epsilon |G|$ elements of $A$ cannot make it bi-induced-$F$-free. A uniform random map is a map $\phi \colon V(F) \to G$ chosen uniformly from all such maps, and it **bi-induces** $F$ when

$$
\phi(u)+\phi(v) \in A \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad uv \in E(F)
$$

for every edge-pair $(u,v) \in U \times V$ of the bipartition of $F$.

**Arbitrary-group induced removal conjecture.** For every $0 < \epsilon < 1/2$, if $A \subseteq G$ is $\epsilon$-far from bi-induced-$F$-free, then

$$
\Pr_{\phi \colon V(F) \to G}[\phi\text{ bi-induces }F] \geq \epsilon^{O_F(1)}.
$$

This would extend the removal lemma from abelian groups to arbitrary groups. The claim is stated as open even for general abelian groups, and therefore remains open in the full arbitrary-group setting.

parsed.title: The bunkbed conjecture for independent bond percolation
parsed.statement:
The bunkbed graph $G=(V,E)$ of a graph $\widetilde{G}=(\widetilde{V},\widetilde{E})$ is formed by superposing two identical copies of $\widetilde{G}$ and adding edges between corresponding vertices. Write $G=\widetilde{G}\times\{0,1\}$. A vertex $(x,0)$ is in the bottom graph, a vertex $(x,1)$ is in the top graph, and the symmetrical vertex of $u=(x,i)$ is $u'=(x,1-i)$. **The bunkbed conjecture.** Let $u$ and $v$ be vertices of the bottom graph, and let $v'$ be the symmetrical vertex of $v$. For every $p\in[0,1]$, independent bond percolation on $G$ satisfies

$$
\mathbb{P}_{p}(u\leftrightarrow v)\geqslant\mathbb{P}_{p}(u\leftrightarrow v').
$$

The conjecture compares the probability of connecting two vertices on the same level with the probability of connecting corresponding vertices on opposite levels. It is known for some subclasses, including outerplanar and wheel graphs; for the complete graph, the paper proves the claim for $p\geqslant 1/2$, while the general statement remains open.

parsed.title: The ultimate periodicity conjecture for super-monochromatic factorisations
parsed.statement:
Let $x$ be an infinite word over an alphabet $\mathcal{A}$. A **super-monochromatic factorisation** of a suffix of $x$ is a factorisation into finite words such that all factors and every ordered concatenation of factors have the same color. **Ultimate periodicity conjecture.** The word $x$ is ultimately periodic if and only if, for every coloring of the set of finite words over $\mathcal{A}$, $x$ admits a suffix having a super-monochromatic factorisation.

The conjecture links ultimate periodicity of infinite words with colorings that avoid monochromatic factorisations of suffixes, subject to the additional requirement that ordered concatenations remain monochromatic. The paper establishes reductions and verifies the conjecture for squarefree words using the notion of consecutive length; the general statement remains open.

parsed.statement: Let $\textbf{T}(n,k)$ denote the set of strings of length $n$ over the paper's alphabet, and let $\textbf{S}\subseteq\textbf{T}(n,k)$ be closed under rotations. This proposes a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the rotation-closed languages for which the FKM algorithm produces a universal cycle.

parsed.title: The $K$-theoretic coefficient-sum conjecture for glides and kaons
parsed.statement:
A weak composition is a finite sequence of nonnegative integers. For weak compositions $a$ and $b$, let $M^a_b(\beta)$ be the coefficient of the glide polynomial $\overline{\mathfrak{F}}_b$ in the glide expansion of the quasiLascoux polynomial $\overline{\mathfrak{Q}}_a$, and let $Q^a_b(\beta)$ be the coefficient of the kaon $\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_b$ in the kaon expansion of the Lascoux atom $\overline{\mathfrak{A}}_a$. Both are nonnegative monomials in $\beta$. **The coefficient-sum conjecture.** For every weak composition $a$,

$$
\sum_b M^a_b(-1)\in\{0,1\}\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_b Q^a_b(-1)\in\{0,1\},
$$

where both sums range over all weak compositions $b$. These conjectures seek geometric interpretations of the relevant $K$-theoretic polynomials and of the coefficient sums as Euler characteristics; no cohomological analogue is expected.

parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $P$ be the path on $n$ vertices. For a labeling $f$ of $G$, write

$$
\operatorname{Range}(f)=\max_{u,v\in V(G)} f(u)-f(v).

$$
\mathbb{E}_{f\in\mathcal{F}(G)}\operatorname{Range}(f)\leq\mathbb{E}_{f\in\mathcal{F}(P)}\operatorname{Range}(f),
$$

and the strong conjecture asserts

$$
\mathbb{P}_{f\in\mathcal{F}(G)}\bigl(\operatorname{Range}(f)\geq k\bigr)\leq\mathbb{P}_{f\in\mathcal{F}(P)}\bigl(\operatorname{Range}(f)\geq k\bigr)
$$

for all $k$. These conjectures ask whether the path maximizes the expected range and, more strongly, stochastically dominates the range distribution among graph-indexed random walks on connected graphs with the same number of vertices. Define the triangle diagram at the critical probability by

$$
\nabla_{p_c}(v)=\sum_{u,w\in V}\mathbb P_{p_c}(v\leftrightarrow u)\mathbb P_{p_c}(u\leftrightarrow w)\mathbb P_{p_c}(w\leftrightarrow v).
$$

**Triangle-condition conjecture.** For every $v\in V$,

$$
\nabla_{p_c}(v)<\infty.

parsed.title: The triangle condition for critical percolation on nonamenable graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, locally finite, nonamenable, quasi-transitive graph, and let $\mathbb P_p(u\leftrightarrow v)$ denote the probability that $u$ and $v$ are connected in Bernoulli bond percolation at parameter $p$. Define the triangle diagram at the critical probability by

$$
\nabla_{p_c}(v)=\sum_{u,w\in V}\mathbb P_{p_c}(v\leftrightarrow u)\mathbb P_{p_c}(u\leftrightarrow w)\mathbb P_{p_c}(w\leftrightarrow v).
$$

**Triangle-condition conjecture.** For every $v\in V$,

$$
\nabla_{p_c}(v)<\infty.
$$

The triangle condition is a standard sufficient condition for mean-field critical exponents, including the expected exponents for cluster volume and percolation probability. It is known in several special cases but remains completely open for general nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs.

parsed.title: The extremal configuration conjecture for d+1 unit vectors
parsed.statement:
Let $d\geqslant 1$, and let $(u_i)_{i=1}^{d+1}$ be a configuration of unit vectors in $S^{d-1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. A sequence of signs is an element $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^{d+1}$. A linear subspace $H\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is even dimensional when $\dim H$ is even.

**Extremal configuration conjecture.** For every such configuration, there exists $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^{d+1}$ such that

$$
\left|\sum_{i=1}^{d+1}\varepsilon_i u_i\right|\geqslant\sqrt{d+2}.
$$

Moreover, equality in the sharp estimate occurs if and only if, up to sign changes, $(u_i)_{i=1}^{d+1}$ is the union of the vertex set of a regular simplex centered at the origin in an even-dimensional linear subspace $H$ and an orthonormal basis of $H^\perp$. This conjecture concerns the extremal point configurations for the corresponding sign-maximization problem; the source notes that the statement was corrected in the cited literature, while its resolution is not specified here.

parsed.title: The coefficient formula for Leibniz graphs in the factorizing operator
parsed.statement:
Let $c_n$ be the coefficients in the factorizing operator

$$
\Diamond=2\cdot\sum_{n\geqslant1}\frac{\hbar^n}{n!}\cdot c_n\cdot\mathcal{F}_{n-1}\bigl([\![{\mathcal{P},\mathcal{P}}]\!],\mathcal{P},\ldots,\mathcal{P}\bigr),
$$

where $w_\Gamma$ is the weight of a Leibniz graph $\Gamma$ and $\#\!\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$ denotes the order of its automorphism group. **The coefficient formula for Leibniz graphs.** For all $n\geqslant2$,

$$
c_n=\frac{n}{3!}=\frac{n}{6},
$$

and consequently the coefficient of the marker $\Gamma$ for the equivalence class $[\Gamma]$ is

$$
2^n\cdot\frac{w_\Gamma}{\#\!\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)}.
$$

This formula is supported by the experiments described in the source, but it remains to be explained how it follows from the $L_\infty$ condition; establishing that derivation would clarify the relation between the formality morphism and associativity of the star product.

parsed.title: The Delta Conjecture, valley version
parsed.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $k$ satisfy $k\leq n$. Let $\mathcal{M P F}_{n,k}$ be the set of valley-marked parking functions of size $n$ with $k$ marked valleys and labels $[n]$. For such a parking function, let $\operatorname{area}$, $\operatorname{dinv}$, and $\operatorname{ides}$ denote its area, marked diagonal-inversion, and inverse-descent statistics, respectively. Let $e_n$ be the elementary symmetric function, let $\Delta'_{e_{n-k-1}}$ denote the primed Delta operator indexed by $e_{n-k-1}$, and let $F_{\operatorname{ides}}$ be the fundamental quasisymmetric function indexed by the inverse-descent set. **The Delta Conjecture, valley version.** For all $k\leq n$, 

$$
\Delta'_{e_{n-k-1}}e_n=\sum_{M P F\in\mathcal{M P F}_{n,k}}t^{\operatorname{area}(M P F)}q^{\operatorname{dinv}(M P F)}F_{\operatorname{ides}(M P F)}.
$$

This is one of the principal combinatorial formulations of the Delta Conjecture; the case $z=0$ recovers the Shuffle Theorem. Many special cases have been proved, but the general conjecture remains open.

parsed.title: Transitive formal-codegree conjecture for fusion categories
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a fusion category. A **formal codegree** is a scalar associated to a formal codegree of $\mathcal{C}$; write $f$ for one such formal codegree. The categories $\mathcal{T}_{\kappa_j}^{\sigma_j}$ are the categories appearing in the stated classification of modular tensor categories with transitive Galois action on their formal-codegree sets, and $\boxtimes$ denotes their Deligne tensor product.

**Formal-codegree conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ has a formal codegree $f$ such that for all $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq2}$, $m$ does not divide $f$, then $\mathcal{C}$ is equivalent to a fusion category of the form

$$
\boxtimes_{j=1}^n\mathcal{T}_{\kappa_j}^{\sigma_j}.
$$

This would extend the announced classification from modular tensor categories to arbitrary fusion categories. The source presents it as a conjectural extension, and no resolution is supplied here.

parsed.title: The balanced-partition conjecture for the $\mathsf a;q$-down-degree expectation
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathsf a$ and $q$ be indeterminates. For a balanced partition $\lambda$, write $w=\lambda_1$ for its width, $\ell=\ell(\lambda)$ for its length, and $d=\gcd(w,\ell)$. Define

$$
W_{\mathsf a;q}(n)=\frac{1-\mathsf a q^{1+2n}}{1-\mathsf a q}q^{-n},\qquad [n]_{\mathsf a;q}=\frac{(1-q^n)(1-\mathsf a q^n)}{(1-q)(1-\mathsf a q)}q^{1-n}.
$$

For $x,y\in[\emptyset,\lambda]$ with $y\lessdot x$, if $y$ is obtained by deleting a cell in row $s$, set

$$
\operatorname{wt}(x,y)=W_{\mathsf a q^{\frac{w+\ell}{d}};q}\left(\frac{w(s-1)+\ell(|x|-1)}{d}\right).
$$

Define

$$
\operatorname{ddeg}_{\mathsf a;q}(x)=\sum_{y\lessdot x}\operatorname{wt}(x,y),
$$

with the sum over $y\in[\emptyset,\lambda]$, and

$$
R(\lambda\mid\mathsf a;q)=\sum_{x\in[\emptyset,\lambda]}W_{\mathsf a q^{\frac{w\ell}{d}};q}\left(\frac{\ell|x|}{d}\right),
$$

so that

$$
\mathbb E_{\mathsf a;q}(X)=\frac{\sum_{x\in[\emptyset,\lambda]}\operatorname{ddeg}_{\mathsf a;q}(x)}{R(\lambda\mid\mathsf a;q)}.
$$

**Balanced-partition product conjecture.** If $\lambda$ is balanced, then

$$
\mathbb E_{\mathsf a;q}(X)=\frac{\left[\frac{w\ell}{d}\right]_{\mathsf a q^{\frac{w+\ell}{d}};q}}{\left[\frac{w+\ell}{d}\right]_{\mathsf a q^{\frac{w\ell}{d}};q}}.
$$

This is an $\mathsf a;q$-analogue of the down-degree expectation formula. The source presents it as a conjecture for balanced partitions of arbitrary slope; no resolution is supplied.

parsed.title: Generalised Alspach conjecture for decompositions into double-rays and Hamiltonian circles
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2k$-regular Cayley graph of an abelian group. For an integer $i$, say that $G$ satisfies condition $P_i$ when every finite cut $F$ with two infinite components satisfies

$$
|F|\equiv i\pmod 2.
$$

**Generalised Alspach conjecture.** If $G$ satisfies condition $P_i$, then $G$ has a decomposition into $i$ Hamiltonian double-rays and $k-i$ Hamiltonian circles. Here a Hamiltonian double-ray is a spanning two-way infinite path, while a Hamiltonian circle is the corresponding topological generalisation of a Hamiltonian cycle in an infinite graph. The parity condition is motivated by the fact that finite cuts with two infinite components must have parity matching the number of double-rays in such a decomposition; the paper establishes the claim in the $4$-regular case, while the stated general form remains open.

parsed.title: The LMAX extension of the set-valued Wilf-equivalence problem
parsed.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of indecomposable patterns. Let $\mathsf{LMAX}$ denote the set-valued statistic recording left-to-right maxima, and let $\mathsf{iar}$ and $\mathsf{comp}$ denote the initial ascending run length and number of components, respectively. **LMAX extension conjecture.** For every $n$,

$$
\left|\mathfrak{S}_n(P)^{\mathsf{LMAX},\mathsf{iar}}\right|=\left|\mathfrak{S}_n(P)^{\mathsf{LMAX},\mathsf{comp}}\right|
\Longleftrightarrow
\left|\mathfrak{S}_n(P)^{\mathsf{LMAX},\mathsf{iar},\mathsf{comp}}\right|=\left|\mathfrak{S}_n(P)^{\mathsf{LMAX},\mathsf{comp},\mathsf{iar}}\right|.
$$

The paper presents this as a suspected special case of an open problem concerning any totally $\oplus$-compatible set-valued statistic, and notes that it is expected to hold for $\mathsf{LMAX}$; no proof or resolution is supplied.

parsed.title: The coprime forest conjecture for friends-and-strangers graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be graphs on $n$ vertices. A graph is **biconnected** if it is connected and has no cut vertex. Write $\overline{Y}$ for the complement of $Y$, and let $\operatorname{FS}(X,Y)$ denote the friends-and-strangers graph associated to $X$ and $Y$. Suppose that

$$
\overline{Y}=\mathscr T_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathscr T_r
$$

is a forest whose components are trees, with

$$
\gcd\bigl(|V(\mathscr T_1)|,\ldots,|V(\mathscr T_r)|\bigr)=1.
$$

**Coprime forest conjecture.** If $X$ is biconnected, then $\operatorname{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected.

This conjecture asserts that the necessary condition obtained from the cycle case is also sufficient for every biconnected graph $X$. The paper verifies the property for several choices of $Y$, including when the complement is a tree on $n-1$ vertices together with an isolated vertex, but the general assertion is left open.
